item.title: Fixing Keycloak's "HTTPS required" behind cloudflared and Envoy Gateway
item.description:
In my Kubernetes cluster, public services are exposed through a Cloudflare Tunnel: cloudflared runs in the cluster and forwards requests to Envoy Gateway, which routes them to the applications. When I published Keycloak this way, every page answered with a 403 and the message “HTTPS required”, although the browser was on https://. item.title: Tailnet-only services with Envoy Gateway, Cloudflare DNS and Tailscale
item.description:
Some services in my Kubernetes cluster, like HashiCorp Vault, should only be reachable from devices on my Tailscale tailnet. They used to be exposed through NodePorts on the node’s Tailscale IP, which works but means remembering port numbers. This article shows how to give them proper hostnames through Envoy Gateway while keeping them off the internet and the LAN.

Three pieces are involved:

  • Cloudflare DNS: a public record pointing at the node’s Tailscale IP
  • Tailscale: split DNS, so devices can resolve that record wherever they are
  • Envoy Gateway: a dedicated listener, restricted by client IP

item.title: Vaultwarden hiding Email 2FA behind a Cloudflare tunnel
item.description:
I run a Vaultwarden instance that can be reached through two hostnames: one goes through a Cloudflare tunnel, the other through a router port forward straight to Envoy Gateway. After configuring SMTP so that users could enable two-step login by email, the Email option appeared in the web vault’s two-step login settings (/#/settings/security/two-factor) on the second hostname, but not on the first.
